question.worked_solution:
We multiply each term inside the parentheses by the term outside the parentheses, simplify using the rules of exponents, and then we add the results together:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}a(9{a}^{4}-15a) & = \\ (\frac{1}{3}a)(9{a}^{4})+(\frac{1}{3}a)(-15a) & = \\ (\frac{1}{3}\cdot 9)({a}^{1}\cdot {a}^{4})+(\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-15))(a\cdot a) & = \\ (3)({a}^{1+4})+(-5)({a}^{1+1}) & = \\ 3{a}^{5}-5{a}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
